`mv`: move or rename files.

## Synopsis

<strong>mv</strong> <em>from to</em>\
<strong>mv</strong> <em>from</em>... <em>directory</em>

## Description

<strong>mv</strong> renames <em>from</em> to <em>to</em>. If the last operand is a directory, each <em>from</em> is moved into it, keeping its name; with more than two operands, the last must be a directory.

Files and directories (with everything in them) can be moved. Across filesystems (between disks, or to <em>/tmp</em>), <strong>mv</strong> copies, then removes the original; symbolic links are copied as links.

## Exit status

0 if everything was moved; 1 on too few operands, a last operand that is not a directory when it must be, or if anything could not be moved.

## Notes

There are no options: every word is a file name.

## See also

<strong>cp</strong>(1), <strong>rm</strong>(1), <strong>ln</strong>(1)
